summary: Module 4 BREAK: investigated the single-core CPU spike on POST /links with long repeating-character URLs using tools only. cProfile of a 5000-char repeating URL showed 0.055s total dominated by test harness, with no app hot spot. Live latency scaling probe across 25..100,019-char URLs showed linear growth (7ms at 10k chars, 16.5ms at 100k chars) -- no super-linear blowup, so no catastrophic backtracking. Regex audit confirms no ambiguous-quantifier regex exists on the URL path (validation is urllib.parse, linear; the only regexes are character classes). The canonical ReDoS bug is structurally absent in this fork. However the profiling data exposed the same bug CLASS: long_url had no max_length, so CPU/memory scale linearly with attacker-controlled input -- an unbounded-input resource-exhaustion vector matching the reported symptom. Fix applied: CreateLinkRequest.long_url now Field(max_length=2048). Verified: 2048 accepted, 2049 rejected with string_too_long, full suite 74 tests exit 0, server restarted healthy.
